1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to when we support a participant who has a . It is for participants, their families and advocates, our workers, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every participant we support who has a tracheostomy, in any setting: their home, a shared home, respite, a day program or the community.
  • Every worker, contractor and agency worker who gives, rosters or oversees this support. A volunteer gives no tracheostomy care. A volunteer calls 000 and gives first aid in an emergency.
  • Every participant who also uses a ventilator. POL-HID-07 Ventilator Management Policy applies to them as well.

This policy applies because [Provider name]'s certificate of registration lists tracheostomy management (, Schedule 2, clause 5(1)). We may not give a Schedule 2 support that is not on our certificate (Practice Standards Rules, section 13C). POL-HID-01 High Intensity Daily Personal Activities Policy sets the commitments every high intensity support shares.

3Commitments

C1

We will make each participant a partner in the assessment and in the for their tracheostomy care. We ask for their consent to the assessment, to health reviews and to sharing their plan. We use their way of communicating, offer an advocate, and record how they took part and what they want.

4Ground rules

G1

The practitioner decides every clinical matter. A worker, a manager or the Clinical Lead never sets, changes, rounds or estimates a value in a plan.

G2

Every clinical value lives in the participant's own plan: a pressure, a depth, a time, a size, a reading or a frequency. Our documents print none as a general rule.

G3

Where the plan and one of our documents differ, the plan applies. The Clinical Lead is told the same day.

G4

In any we call 000 first. We call the practitioner, the manager and the family after.

G5

A worker does a task only if their sign-off lists it, for this participant. Every worker may give first aid, give CPR and call 000. A worker whose training does not cover CPR for a person with a tracheostomy gives chest compressions only, with 000 on speaker, and keeps the stoma uncovered. Stoma or tube breaths are given by a worker trained for this participant, as the plan's resuscitation page says.

G6

Only the practitioner plans a tube change. Ties are changed by the practitioner with a second person, as the skills descriptor sets. Where the practitioner's plan names two signed-off workers to change the ties together, and the law of [state or territory] allows it, they may do so as the plan sets. Nobody changes ties alone.

G7

We use only the tube, catheters, solutions and equipment the plan names. We never put water or saline into the tube unless the plan prescribes it.

G8

We suction when the participant shows a sign the plan lists, or asks for it. We use a time set by the clock only where the plan sets one and says why.

G9

A hold or a device used to stop a participant moving, to protect the tube, can be a regulated restrictive practice. The Service Manager checks PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure before any is used.

G10

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader cannot be their own Clinical Lead and cannot sign off their own competency. They engage a registered nurse, or another health practitioner whose scope covers tracheostomy care, for both. A person outside the business does the clinical review of an incident. A sole trader needs a second signed-off person before taking on a participant.

G11

The law of [state or territory] on who may carry out a clinical task, and who may delegate it, applies. Where it is stricter than this policy, the law governs.

suction

emergency kit
the bag or box of spare tubes, ties, catheters, suction and other items the plan lists. It stays with the participant.

any event in which the participant cannot get enough air through the tube, the stoma, the mouth or the nose.

the signed-off worker who steadies the tube and helps at a tie or dressing change. Nobody changes ties alone.

the manager who takes workers' calls. In office hours this is the Service Manager. After hours it is the rostered manager. A clinical question goes to the participant's practitioner, or to the Clinical Lead.

This procedure gives effect to POL-HID-05 Tracheostomy Management Policy, C1 to C14.

In this procedure:

  • the plan: the participant's tracheostomy plan, written by their practitioner and held with FRM-HID-01 Participant Health Support Plan.
  • the : the NDIS Commission's High Intensity Support Skills Descriptor for tracheostomy support.
  • the : the National Disability Insurance Scheme ( Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • the Restrictive Practices Rules: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

2When and who

Start at step 1 when a participant with a tracheostomy asks us for support. Start there too when a participant we already support has a tracheostomy placed. After a new tracheostomy or a tube change, care by our workers starts or restarts only from the date the practitioner writes in the plan, with any extra rule the practitioner sets for that period. Steps 10 to 20 run every shift. Steps 21 to 26 run the moment an airway emergency starts. Steps 27 to 30 run after an event, at each review, every week and every month.

A tracheostomy is an opening in the neck, called a stoma, that holds a tube so the participant can breathe. An airway emergency is any event in which the participant cannot get enough air through the tube, the stoma, the mouth or the nose. Decision table 2 lists the signs.

Who acts:

  • The is a registered nurse, or another health practitioner whose scope covers tracheostomy care, whom we engage to oversee this support. They arrange the practitioner's assessment and check the plan. They set the training plan, review incidents, book reviews, read a sample of the care record every month, and read every record after an incident or a plan change.
  • The participant's health practitioner assesses the participant, writes and reviews the plan, and decides every clinical value in it. This is a medical practitioner, nurse practitioner, registered nurse or other health practitioner whose training and scope cover tracheostomy care. They are the participant's own, not our employee.
  • The trains each worker and signs off each task. This is the practitioner, or a person who meets the skills descriptor for tracheostomy support. The Clinical Lead checks their qualification first.
  • The Service Manager asks for the participant's consent, rosters , puts the plan where workers can reach it, and checks every care record for completeness each week. In office hours the Service Manager is also the .
  • The worker on shift cares for the participant under the plan. A signed-off worker has a for this participant in REG-HID-01 High Intensity Training and Competency Register. It lists the tasks they may do, and it covers one participant only.
  • The on-call manager takes workers' calls at any hour: the Service Manager in office hours, the rostered manager after hours. A clinical question goes to the practitioner, or to the Clinical Lead.
  • The authorised notifier, who is the Quality Manager, decides whether an incident is reportable.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader is the Service Manager, the on-call manager and the worker on shift. A sole trader cannot be their own Clinical Lead or trainer, and cannot sign off their own competency. They engage a registered nurse, or another health practitioner whose scope covers tracheostomy care, for both. Three tasks are never done by the sole trader alone: the plan check at step 4, which the engaged Clinical Lead does with the participant's practitioner; the sign-off at step 7, which the practitioner or another trainer does; and the clinical review at step 28, which a person outside the business does. A sole trader who is the only signed-off worker has no cover. They need a second signed-off person for the tasks that need two, and for leave, and name that person at Q77 before taking on the participant. Where a step says to phone the on-call manager, a sole trader phones the practitioner and writes down the time. A sole trader checks their own record for completeness each week and sends a copy to the engaged Clinical Lead every month, who does the sample read at step 30 (our standard).

4Watch out

  • Call 000 first in an airway emergency. A blocked or displaced tube can stop breathing within minutes. A call to the practitioner or a manager first costs time the participant does not have.
  • Never force a catheter or a tube. Force can tear the airway or push a blockage deeper.
  • takes air as well as secretions. Suction that is too long, too deep or too hard can drop the participant's oxygen and injure the airway. Use only the limits in the plan.
  • Never change the ties alone. One person changing ties can let the tube come out. The practitioner changes them with you as the , or two signed-off workers the plan names change them together. Nobody changes them alone.
  • A valve or cap on a tube with an inflated cuff can stop breathing out. Fit one only as the plan says.
  • Water or loose material near the stoma can be breathed in. A shower, a bath, a bib, powder or fluff can block the airway, cause an infection or drown the participant. Follow the plan's rules for water and for covering the stoma.
  • Do only what you are signed off for. A task done without a sign-off can harm the participant. It can also breach the Code of Conduct duty to give safe and competent support.
  • Never guess a value. A value from memory, or from another participant's plan, can be wrong for this participant. Read Section A.
  • A change in secretions, a new smell or any blood can be the first sign of trouble. Report it straight away, during the shift. Waiting until the end of the shift can cost the participant their airway.
  • Never restrain a participant to give care. Force can harm them, and a hold or device used to stop their movement may be a restrictive practice.

Keep the airway open and stay with the participant until help comes.

If step 21 is not done, tell a second person to call 000 now. Keep the participant sitting up if they are awake, unless the plan says otherwise. Do not push the tube back in. The one exception is a worker the plan names at Q37 for putting in a spare tube, who is signed off. That worker uses the spare the plan names, and the smaller size if it will not go in. Stop at once if you meet any resistance. If you are not named, put nothing into the stoma. Then follow the branch for this participant at Q9. Q9 says YES, air passes through the mouth and nose: keep the participant calm, watch their breathing, and cover the stoma only if the plan's page says to. Q9 says NO, the participant breathes only through the neck: never cover the stoma, keep it clear, and give oxygen at the stoma if the plan has it and you are signed off. Q9 says PARTLY: follow the plan's page for this participant. If the participant stops breathing, go to step 25. Keep the tube that came out for the crew.

Result
The participant is breathing, or is supported until the crew arrives. A spare tube is put in only by a worker the plan names.
Record
FRM-HID-08 Q70
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Step 24

The worker on shift

If Blood comes from the tube or stoma, or is in the secretions, and is more than the plan's streak or does not stop:

Stay with the participant, keep the airway open and act on where the blood comes from.

Call 000 first (step 21). Keep the participant upright if they are awake, unless the plan says otherwise. Blood from the skin at the edge of the stoma: press a clean pad gently on the skin beside the stoma, never over the tube opening or the stoma. Blood from inside the tube: press nothing; sit the participant up, keep the airway clear with suction only if you are signed off and the airway is filling, and tell the 000 operator that blood is coming from inside the tube. Never take the tube out. Keep any soaked pads, and tell the crew when the bleeding started. If the participant stops breathing, go to step 25. A streak of blood within the plan's limit goes to step 19.

Result
The airway stays open, bleeding at the skin is pressed, and help is coming.
Record
FRM-HID-08 Q70
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 3Policy C3Record it on: →Form, question 70Form Q70

Step 25

The worker on shift

If The participant does not respond, or is only gasping:

Check for breathing, and start CPR if it is not normal.

Check for a response and for breathing. If the participant does not respond but is breathing normally, do not start compressions. Place them in the recovery position as you were trained, keep the stoma clear and uncovered, and watch their breathing until the crew arrives. If they are not breathing, or only gasping, send for the defibrillator and start chest compressions straight away, as you were trained. Give breaths where the plan's resuscitation page says: through the tube, at the stoma, or at the mouth and nose with the stoma covered. Use the resuscitation bag in the kit as your CPR training for this participant covered. If your training does not cover CPR for a person with a tracheostomy, give chest compressions only, keep the stoma uncovered and follow the 000 operator. If the tube is blocked and you cannot clear it, the plan's resuscitation page says what to do with the breaths, and step 22 says which tasks a named worker may do. Use the defibrillator as the machine directs. Keep going until the crew takes over, the participant moves or breathes, or you cannot go on. Do not stop to look for the plan. Tell the crew about any advance care directive. If the plan holds a signed decision not to resuscitate, its page says what to do. If you have no such page, start CPR.

Result
The participant gets the right help without delay, CPR or the recovery position, until the crew takes over.
Record
FRM-HID-08 Q70
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

Step 26

The worker on shift

If The suction unit, the humidifier or other equipment fails, or the power goes out, while the participant needs it:

Switch to the backup in the plan.

If suction fails, use the backup at Q36. If the humidifier fails, use the backup humidification the plan names. If the power goes, move to battery equipment and check each item is on. Phone the on-call manager. If no backup works and the participant needs suction or shows a sign in Decision table 2, call 000 (step 21). If the participant also uses a ventilator, follow PRO-HID-06 Ventilator Management Procedure as well. If the home must be left, follow FRM-SUP-07 Participant Emergency and Disaster Plan and take the kit and the plan. Keep the faulty item out of use until it is fixed, and tell the Service Manager the same day.

Result
The participant keeps the care they need, or help is coming.
Record
FRM-HID-08 Q48 and Q70
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)

After an event, at each review, every week and every month

Step 27

The worker on shift

Report the event to the on-call manager, then write the incident report.

Do this after any airway emergency, call to 000, tube out, error or near miss. Do it too after a blocked tube that needed more than the usual suction. Do it too after a worker is splashed or pricked by secretions or blood. For a splash or a prick, wash the area with soap and water and rinse the eyes with clean water, then seek medical assessment straight away, within hours and not at the end of the day. It is also a work health and safety incident. Phone the on-call manager as soon as the participant is safe. Complete the incident report form (FRM-INC-01) before your shift ends, and record the incident type as a health emergency. Write what you saw, did and said, in the order it happened. Say if the participant went to hospital. The Quality Manager, as the authorised notifier, decides whether it is reportable under PRO-INC-02 Reportable Incidents Notification Procedure, and notifies the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware where the incident involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm; otherwise within 5 business days. Tell the practitioner straight away, during the shift. Write the report number at Q71 and keep any used equipment. The on-call manager tells the Clinical Lead, and the people the participant chose are told as PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure sets.

Result
The on-call manager knows, PRO-INC-01 has started and the report number is on the record.
Record
FRM-INC-01 (incident type); FRM-HID-08 Q71
Time limit
Phone as soon as the participant is safe (our standard). Write before your shift ends (our standard). A worker must tell a manager of a reportable incident as soon as possible (statutory: the Incident Rules, section 19)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 13Policy C13Record it on: →Form, question 71Form Q71

Step 28

The Clinical Lead

Review the incident clinically, and ask the practitioner for their review.

Read the incident report and the care record for the shifts before it. Ask what the participant's breathing, secretions and readings showed in the days before. Ask whether the plan, the equipment, the training or the roster played a part. Ask the practitioner to review the plan and the participant, and record the date you asked. Ask whether any worker needs to be assessed again (Decision table 4). PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure asks for the participant's own views. Write each action with an owner and a date in the incident assessment (FRM-INC-01). Support the worker. Reporting is never punished.

Result
The cause is understood, the plan is reviewed where it needs to be, and every action has an owner and a date.
Record
FRM-INC-01 (clinical review and actions); REG-HID-02
Time limit
The Clinical Lead's review within 1 business day of the incident, and the same day when it needed 000. The practitioner's review is asked for within 1 business day (our standard)

Step 29

The Clinical Lead

Act on Decision table 4.

Check REG-HID-02 every week for review dates coming due. Book the practitioner's review at the interval at Q8, and whenever a row in Decision table 4 applies. Ask the participant what is working, what they want changed and whether they want an advocate there. Ask workers whether the plan is meeting the participant's needs (Q72). Send the practitioner the care record. After the review, the practitioner updates the plan. Then repeat step 4 for the changed answers and step 9 for the copies. Book worker assessments that a row calls for. Record the review and the date of the next one.

Result
The review or assessment is booked and held, the participant's views are recorded, and the plan and Section A match again.

As Decision table 4 sets for each row (our standard)

Step 30

The Service Manager, then the Clinical Lead

Check the care record for completeness each week, and read a sample each month.

Service Manager, every week: check every shift's entries for answers left blank or written as ticks, missed kit checks, and tasks initialled by a worker whose sign-off does not list them. Phone the worker about each gap. Clinical Lead, every month: read a sample of the participant's records, and every record after an incident or a plan change. Look for readings outside the limits that nobody reported, and for changes in secretions or skin across the days. If the record shows a trend, ask the practitioner for a review. Send trends to the Quality Manager for the 3 month audit.

Result
Every gap in completeness is found within a week, every clinical trend within a month, and each has an action.
Record
FRM-HID-08 Q74
Time limit
Every week for completeness. Every month for the sample, and after every incident or plan change (our standard)

6Decision

Decision table 1: who may do what (steps 7, 16, 17, 22 and 23). It follows the skills descriptor for tracheostomy support. Where the law of [state or territory] is stricter, follow the law.

If the task isThen
First aid, CPR and calling 000Every worker on shift. First aid and CPR must be current
Check the plan, the kit and the equipment. Take the observations the plan asks for. Record each shiftA signed-off worker
Suction through the tube, with the catheter, pressure, depth, time and technique the plan setsOnly a worker signed off for suction for this participant
Clean the stoma and the skin. Give mouth care. Keep humidification as the plan setsA signed-off worker
Check, clean or replace the inner cannulaOnly a worker the plan names at Q37 and whose sign-off lists it. Otherwise the practitioner
Fit or remove a speaking valve or a capOnly a worker the plan names at Q37 and whose sign-off lists it. Otherwise the practitioner
Measure the cuff pressure, or inflate or deflate the cuff for routine careThe practitioner. A worker only if the plan names them at Q37 and their sign-off lists it
Deflate the cuff before a speaking valve or cap, and reinflate it as the plan setsOnly a worker the plan names at Q37 and whose sign-off lists it. A worker not signed off for this step never fits a valve or cap on a cuffed tube
Change a routine stoma dressingThe practitioner. A worker only if the plan names them at Q21 and their sign-off lists it. Otherwise the worker helps as the second person
Change the tracheostomy tiesThe practitioner, with a signed-off worker as the second person. Where the plan names two signed-off workers to change the ties together, and the law of [state or territory] allows it, those two workers as the plan sets. Never one person alone
Change the tube as planned, change its type or size, or decide to cap, downsize or remove itOnly the practitioner
Put in a spare tube during an emergencyOnly a worker the plan names at Q37 and whose sign-off lists it. Otherwise nobody. Call 000
Deflate the cuff in a blocked tube emergencyOnly a worker the plan names at Q37 and whose sign-off lists it, in the order and the way the plan's blocked tube page sets. Otherwise nobody. Call 000
Remove a blocked tube that cannot be cleared, where Q9 says air passes through the mouth and noseOnly a worker the plan names at Q37 and whose sign-off lists it, in the order and the way the plan's blocked tube page sets. Otherwise nobody. Call 000
Give oxygen or a nebulised treatmentOxygen is a prescribed medicine: give it only at the flow the plan prescribes, by a signed-off worker, and record it on the medication chart as PRO-MED-01 Management of Medication Procedure sets. A nebulised treatment is the same
Set or change a suction pressure, depth, time or frequency, or any other value in the planOnly the practitioner
Judge the chest, decide the cause of an infection or a blockage, or decide the participant is wellOnly the practitioner. A worker reports what they see
Work a ventilatorOnly a worker signed off under PRO-HID-06 Ventilator Management Procedure

Decision table 2: signs of an airway emergency (steps 21 to 26). Call 000 first, then follow the step named.

If you seeThen
The participant is not breathing, does not respond, or is only gaspingCall 000 now (step 21). Then start CPR (step 25)
Blue, grey or very pale lips or faceCall 000 now (step 21). Then step 22
Struggling to breathe, noisy breathing that suction does not fix, or no air moving through the tubeCall 000 now (step 21). Then step 22
The suction catheter will not passCall 000 now (step 21). Then step 22
New drowsiness, confusion or trouble waking the participantCall 000 now (step 21). Then step 22
The tube is out or partly outCall 000 now (step 21). Then step 23
Bleeding beyond the streak the plan allows, or bleeding that does not stopCall 000 now (step 21). Then step 24
A sign or a reading on the plan's call 000 list at Q27Call 000 now (step 21)
Suction, the humidifier or the power fails and the participant needs itGo to step 26. Call 000 if no backup works
You are not sure whether it is an emergencyCall 000 now (step 21). A call that was not needed costs nothing

Decision table 3: whom to tell, and how fast (steps 19 and 27).

If you findThen tellHowBy when
Any sign in Decision table 2000, then the on-call managerPhoneStraight away
A value outside the limits at Q25, a change in secretions, any blood within the plan's limit, a new sign of infection at the stoma, or anything on the list at Q28The practitioner. Then the Clinical Lead or the on-call managerPhoneStraight away
Coughing, a wet voice or new secretions after eating or drinkingThe practitionerPhoneStraight away, during the shift
A missing kit item, a flat battery or a faulty suction unitThe on-call managerPhoneBefore you start care
A task due that you are not signed off forThe on-call managerPhoneBefore the task is due
The participant refuses care, or asks for a changeThe practitioner and the Clinical LeadPhone, then Q68 or Q72Straight away, during the shift

Decision table 4: when the practitioner reviews, and when a worker is assessed again (steps 7, 28 and 29).

IfThen the practitionerThen each worker

Care restarts on the hospital discharge summary and the handover record (FRM-SUP-10) where the tube, its size and the suction limits are unchanged. Where any of these changed, care waits for the reviewIs briefed on the discharge summary before their next shift. Is assessed again if the clinical content of the plan changed

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
You are not signed off for a task, or your sign-off has lapsedDo not do the task. Phone the on-call manager before you start. A signed-off worker covers. You may stay, give first aid and call 000. If the participant shows a sign of needing suction and no signed-off worker is there, call 000
No signed-off worker is free for a shiftThe on-call manager phones the cover list, then the Clinical Lead. They tell the participant and the people they chose, and write the gap in the continuity record under PRO-COS-01 Continuity of Supports Procedure (REG-COS-01 Service Disruption and Shift Cover Register, once its Rise version is written). Nobody leaves the participant with a worker who cannot suction when the plan says suction may be needed. Without a signed-off worker the on-call manager asks the practitioner what to do
The plan is missing, out of date, or does not fit how the participant is nowDo not guess. Phone the on-call manager and the practitioner. Give first aid and call 000 if needed. Give no care that the plan does not cover, unless the practitioner tells you to by phone. Write their words
The practitioner cannot be reachedTry the number at Q5 twice in 10 minutes. Then use the after-hours number and the clinic team. Then phone the on-call manager. Call 000 if the participant looks worse
The participant refuses careStop that care and explain what could happen. Ask what they would accept. Never force, trick or bribe them. Stay near. If a sign in Decision table 2 appears, go to step 21. Tell the practitioner straight away, during the shift, and write it at Q68. The Clinical Lead asks the practitioner to review the plan
The participant pulls at the tube or fights suctionStay calm. You may guide a hand away from the tube in a reflexive way to stop harm. You never hold the participant down and never use a device to stop their movement. If the tube is out or moving, go to step 23. Phone the on-call manager. A protective device the treating team prescribes for a clinical purpose, such as a mitt or a splint, is used only as the plan says, and only after the Clinical Lead and a behaviour support practitioner have decided under PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure whether it is a regulated restrictive practice. A hold or a device used to stop a participant's movement to influence their behaviour is a regulated restrictive practice (the Restrictive Practices Rules, section 6). A reflexive guide-away, and a device used for a therapeutic purpose, are excluded (section 6(c) and (d))
The participant cannot tell you what they need, or their aid is missing or brokenUse the other ways at Q32, and stay close. Phone the on-call manager to repair or replace the aid. Start no care that is not urgent until the participant can say yes or no in some way
The kit, the suction unit or the backup is missing or faultyDo not start care that needs it. Phone the on-call manager straight away. They send or replace the item during the shift. If the participant needs suction and none works, call 000
A time limit in this procedure will be missedTell the Clinical Lead before it passes. They set a new time and write the reason in the record at Q74. A time limit in an airway emergency is never moved
The participant goes into hospitalSend the plan, Section A and the emergency pages. Tell the hospital team about the tube and how the participant communicates. Complete FRM-SUP-10 Hospital and Temporary Transition Handover Record. Decision table 4 applies when they come home
The participant goes outThe kit and the suction go with them. Do step 11 before you leave and when you return. Take the plan and the practitioner's numbers
The power fails, or the home must be leftGo to step 26. PLN-EDM-01 Emergency and Disaster Management Plan applies as well
The participant also uses a ventilatorPRO-HID-06 Ventilator Management Procedure applies as well. Record on FRM-HID-10 Ventilator Check and Care Record too. If the two procedures differ outside an emergency, stop and ask the practitioner. In an emergency, follow the emergency steps of this procedure and raise the difference afterwards
This procedure and the plan differThe plan applies. Tell the Clinical Lead the same day
A second person is needed for the ties and none is thereDo not change the ties. Hold the tube steady, keep the participant still and phone the practitioner. They decide who changes them and how. If the tube moves or comes out, go to step 23
A family member or carer asks you to do a task that is not in the plan or your sign-offSay no kindly. Phone the Clinical Lead. Only the practitioner can add a task, and trains the person
You made an errorMake the participant safe. Follow step 27. Reporting is never punished. An assessment after an error is support for you, not a penalty
You think a colleague does tasks they are not signed off for, skips the checks, or writes a record that is not trueTell the Clinical Lead during the same shift. If it is about the Clinical Lead, tell the Chief Executive. You can also phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you. If you think it is abuse or neglect, PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure applies
The concern is about the Chief Executive, or about a sole traderTell the independent contact for concerns named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, or phone the NDIS Commission
The electronic record is downUse the paper record kept at [location at each site]. Enter it in the system within 1 business day of it coming back

8Done means

For each participant, the work is done when all of these are true:

  • the participant has a current plan, made with them and written by a qualified practitioner, and Section A matches it
  • the participant's consent, or their refusal, is recorded
  • every worker who cares for them holds a current sign-off for their tasks
  • every shift has a complete record, with values and not ticks
  • every airway emergency has a call to 000, an incident report and a clinical review
  • the next health review and the next assessment of each worker have dates.

These records now exist:

  • the care record (FRM-HID-08), with Sections A to G complete for the period
  • the plan, its practitioner, the consent, each review and the next review due, in REG-HID-02
  • each worker's training and sign-off, in REG-HID-01
  • an incident report (FRM-INC-01) and a row in REG-INC-01 Incident Register for each event in the Incident Rules
  • the weekly completeness check and the monthly sample read, at Q74, and any action they set.

9Quick card

144 words
  • Not breathing, blue or grey, tube out, tube blocked, or bleeding: call 000 now (step 21)
  • Blocked tube: sit up, take off any valve or cap, suction as the plan sets, never force, then the page's next tasks only if the plan names you (step 22)
  • Tube out: stay, keep the airway open, push nothing in unless the plan names you (step 23)
  • Not breathing: start CPR and give breaths where the plan says (step 25)
  • Bleeding: press beside the stoma, never block the tube (step 24)
  • Suction or power fails: use the backup, and call 000 if none works (step 26)
  • Do only the tasks you are signed off for. Nobody changes ties alone (step 17)
  • Check the kit and the suction before any care, every shift (step 11)
  • Phone the practitioner straight away about any change on the plan's list (step 19)

form.intro:
This record holds one participant's tracheostomy plan in brief, and every shift of care given under it. Keep one record for each participant with a tracheostomy. It gives effect to PRO-HID-04 Tracheostomy Management Procedure and POL-HID-05 Tracheostomy Management Policy.

Who completes it, and when:

  • Section A: the participant's health practitioner completes it with the participant, from the plan. The Clinical Lead checks it. Complete it again whenever the plan changes.
  • Sections B to F: the worker on shift completes these during every shift. Only a worker signed off for a task answers the questions about that task.
  • Section G: the Service Manager completes Q76 and Q77 before the first shift, and checks the record for completeness every week. The Clinical Lead reads a sample every month, and every record after an incident or a plan change. The practitioner reads it at every health review.

Have ready: the plan and its emergency pages, the consent record (FRM-INF-01) and the list of signed-off workers. That list is in REG-HID-01 High Intensity Training and Competency Register.

Rules for the record:

  • Write values, not ticks. A tick does not show what you found.
  • Never copy a value from memory. Copy it from Section A, which comes from the plan.
  • If the plan does not say, write "not in the plan" and phone the practitioner. Never fill the gap yourself.
  • Write in ink, or use an electronic record that locks each entry.
  • Rule one line through a mistake, initial it and write the right entry beside it. Never erase it or write over it.
  • Print the Section A summary (Q1, Q4, Q5, Q9, Q10, Q16 to Q18, Q25 to Q28 and Q31) at the top of every page of the shift chart, and keep the full Section A in the participant's file. Number every page, and file each full page in the participant's file.

Every page carries these lines:

  • Not breathing, blue or grey, tube out, tube blocked, or bleeding beyond the plan's streak: call 000 now.
  • Anything on the plan's list at Q28: phone the practitioner now. The practitioner who set the limits is at Q4, and their numbers are at Q5.
  • Suction or power fails: use the backup at Q36. If none works, call 000.

What happens next: the Service Manager checks the record for completeness every week. The Clinical Lead reads a sample every month, and every record after an incident or a plan change. The practitioner reads it at each health review. PRO-HID-04 Tracheostomy Management Procedure sets every step.

When systems are down, use the paper copy. Paper copies are kept at [location at each site].
form.privacy:
We collect this information so that trained workers give you safe tracheostomy care under your plan. It also shows what was done. It includes health information about you.

The workers who care for you read it. So do the Clinical Lead, the Service Manager and your practitioner. With your consent, we share it with your doctor, other health services and the people you choose. In an emergency we give it to ambulance and hospital staff where the law allows. FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form records your consent.

You can ask to see what we hold about you and ask us to correct it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
